final_note: You worked through Properties of electromagnetic waves 2 — 8 specification statements.

concepts.def: A repeated back-and-forth change in the current in a circuit, so that charge flows first one way and then the other, over and over again. The number of complete back-and-forth cycles each second is the frequency of the oscillation.

(HT only) Radio waves can be produced by oscillations in electrical circuits. A circuit made to oscillate at a chosen frequency drives charge back and forth in a transmitting aerial, and radio waves of that frequency are sent out.

(HT only) When radio waves are absorbed they may create an alternating current in a circuit — a current that repeatedly reverses direction rather than flowing steadily one way. In this sense radio waves can themselves induce oscillations in an electrical circuit.

(HT only) The alternating current created when a radio wave is absorbed has the same frequency as the radio wave itself. A 200 MHz wave absorbed by a receiving aerial sets up an alternating current of 200 MHz in the circuit joined to it.
Gamma rays originate from changes in the nucleus of an atom. They are the part of the electromagnetic spectrum whose source is nuclear rather than a change involving the electrons of the atom.

Changes in atoms and the nuclei of atoms can result in electromagnetic waves being generated or absorbed over a wide frequency range. The same kinds of change work in both directions: an atom able to emit a wave of a given frequency can also absorb one.

Radiation with enough energy to knock electrons out of atoms, leaving charged particles behind. X-rays and gamma rays are ionising radiation, and this is why they can cause the mutation of genes and cancer.

Radiation dose (in sieverts) is a measure of the risk of harm resulting from an exposure of the body to the radiation. It is not a count of waves or of decays: it is a measure of risk, and the harm depends on the type of radiation as well as on the size of the dose.

The two sizes of unit used for radiation dose in this specification are related by 1000 millisieverts (mSv) = 1 sievert (Sv). To change a dose in mSv into Sv, divide by 1000; to change a dose in Sv into mSv, multiply by 1000.
Ultraviolet waves can cause skin to age prematurely and increase the risk of skin cancer. These are the two effects of ultraviolet on human body tissue named by the specification.

A change to a gene inside a cell. X-rays and gamma rays are ionising radiation that can cause the mutation of genes and cancer, so damage from these waves is damage to the material inside cells rather than simple heating of tissue.

To draw a conclusion about risk from a table of doses, first put every dose into the same unit using 1000 mSv = 1 Sv, then compare the numbers. Only once the units match does a larger number mean a larger risk of harm.

mcqs.q: (HT only) How can radio waves be produced?
options: By oscillations in an electrical circuit
By heating a metal aerial till it glows
By changes in the nucleus of the atom
By changes in the electrons of an atom
mcqs.explain: The specification states that radio waves can be produced by oscillations in electrical circuits.

mcqs.q: (HT only) A radio wave is absorbed by an aerial joined to a circuit. What may the wave create in that circuit?
options: A steady direct current, always one way
An alternating current in that circuit
A magnetic field but no current in it
A current whose frequency is doubled
mcqs.explain: The specification states that absorbed radio waves may create an alternating current, so they induce oscillations in the circuit.

mcqs.q: (HT only) A transmitter sends out radio waves at 200 MHz. A receiving aerial absorbs them and an alternating current is created in the circuit joined to it. What is the frequency of that current?
options: 100 MHz, half the frequency of the wave
400 MHz, twice the frequency of the wave
200 MHz, the same as that radio wave
0 Hz, because the current is direct
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the alternating current created has the same frequency as the radio wave itself.

options: In changes to the electrons of an atom
In bonds being broken between two atoms
In the heating of very dense material
In changes in the nucleus of an atom
mcqs.explain: The specification states that gamma rays originate from changes in the nucleus of an atom.

mcqs.q: Which statement about how electromagnetic waves are generated and absorbed is correct?
options: Only changes in the nuclei of atoms can generate these waves
Changes in atoms and in their nuclei generate and absorb them
Only changes in the electrons of an atom can generate them
Atoms generate these waves but can never absorb any of them
mcqs.explain: The specification states that changes in atoms and the nuclei of atoms can result in electromagnetic waves being generated or absorbed over a wide frequency range.

mcqs.q: A worker's radiation dose is recorded in sieverts (Sv). What does this dose measure?
options: The number of nuclei decaying near the worker
The amount of radioactive material in the body
The risk of harm that results from the exposure
The frequency of the radiation entering the body
mcqs.explain: The specification states that radiation dose (in sieverts) is a measure of the risk of harm resulting from an exposure of the body to the radiation.

mcqs.q: Ultraviolet waves, X-rays and gamma rays can have hazardous effects on human body tissue. What do those effects depend on?
options: The size of the dose received, whatever type it is
The type of radiation alone, not the size of dose
The distance the radiation travelled to the body
The type of radiation and the size of the dose
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the effects depend on the type of radiation and the size of the dose.

mcqs.q: A patient receives a radiation dose of 75 mSv from a scan. Use 1000 millisieverts (mSv) = 1 sievert (Sv). What is this dose in sieverts?
options: 7.5 Sv
75 Sv
mcqs.explain: 75 divided by 1000 gives 0.075 Sv, using the relationship 1000 mSv = 1 Sv as given in the stem.

mcqs.q: The table shows the average dose a person in the UK receives each year: radon gas 1.3 mSv, medical X-rays 0.4 mSv, cosmic rays 0.3 mSv. Which conclusion is supported by these data?
options: Medical X-rays give the largest yearly dose of the three
The three sources together give a dose of over one sievert
Radon gives a larger yearly dose than the other two added
Cosmic rays carry the greatest risk as they come from space
mcqs.explain: 1.3 mSv is greater than 0.4 mSv + 0.3 mSv = 0.7 mSv, so this conclusion does follow from the data given.

mcqs.q: Three workers received yearly doses of 6 mSv, 18 mSv and 0.5 Sv. Use 1000 millisieverts (mSv) = 1 sievert (Sv). Which worker is at the greatest risk of harm?
options: The worker on 18 mSv, the largest number shown
The worker on 6 mSv, since small doses build up most
All three equally, as any dose carries one risk
The worker on 0.5 Sv, because that equals 500 mSv
mcqs.explain: Converting with 1000 mSv = 1 Sv gives 500 mSv, far greater than 18 mSv or 6 mSv, so this dose carries the greatest risk.

mcqs.q: What effects can ultraviolet waves have on human body tissue?
options: Skin ages early and the risk of skin cancer rises
Genes mutate, as ultraviolet is ionising radiation
Skin ages early but the risk of cancer is unchanged
Skin ages early because the tissue gets heated
mcqs.explain: The specification states that ultraviolet waves can cause skin to age prematurely and increase the risk of skin cancer.

mcqs.q: Why can X-rays and gamma rays cause cancer in human body tissue?
options: They are absorbed by the skin and make it age early
They are ionising and can cause genes to mutate
They heat body cells until those cells are killed
They are ionising, so they burn the skin surface
mcqs.explain: The specification states that X-rays and gamma rays are ionising radiation that can cause the mutation of genes and cancer.
